summary: Edama V8 full-stack testing (backend + frontend). 20/20 pytest cases pass covering auth (login/me/refresh/401), reconciliation exact counts (2565/57/17/45/1662/118/3760/3403/67/120/9 pending), REVIEW_REQUIRED kinds breakdown (1/3/5), consultant (270 submissions) and evaluator (225 queue, 136h, 5 orgs) scoped endpoints, RBAC 403 cross-role checks, and brute-force 429 lockout after 5 failures. Frontend: RTL Arabic login → admin reconciliation dashboard renders every contract count with green checkmarks and PASS badge, cohort coverage table matches 24/30/29/35 / 0/1200/1160/1400 / 0/1382/1081/940, review-queue lists 9 rows, consultant and evaluator role landings render correctly with their data-testid pages. Discovered and fixed two backend defects to make brute-force lockout actually work (see RCA).

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout was ineffective: (1) datetime comparison crashed with TypeError because MongoDB returns naive datetime while now() is tz-aware, returning 500 instead of 429; (2) identifier was ip:email so multi-pod / proxy deployments (this env shows two client IPs 10.232.130.143/144) reset the counter each request. Fixed both; brute-force now returns 429 on 6th attempt.

issues: Console shows a 401 from an initial /api/auth/me probe before the user has logged in — harmless but noisy; consider suppressing the error toast/log on the unauthenticated bootstrap call.

action_items: Optional: silence the unauthenticated /auth/me 401 log noise on Login page bootstrap.
Optional hardening: also consider capping by IP in addition to email for brute-force to protect against distributed enumeration.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py check_lockout was comparing datetime.now(tz=UTC) with a naive datetime coming back from Mongo — classic tz bug producing 500s. Fix applied to normalise last_at to UTC.

auth_routes.login used identifier=f'{ip}:{email}' which is fragile behind K8s ingress/multi-worker: each request may arrive from a different peer IP, defeating the counter. Switched identifier to email-only for the lockout key.
Consider centralising datetime handling: always store timezone-aware UTC in Mongo (motor stores as naive by default) or wrap all datetime reads in a helper that attaches UTC.

Note that Mongo returns naive datetimes — any new code doing tz-aware arithmetic on stored timestamps must normalise first (see fix in auth.py).
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout not triggering. Reproduction: send 6 POSTs to /api/auth/login with invalid credentials for the same email. Expected: 5×401 then 429. Observed (before fix): 5×401 then 500 with TypeError('can\'t subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes') coming from auth.py:129. Root cause #1: MongoDB (motor) returns stored datetimes as naive, while check_lockout used datetime.now(timezone.utc). Root cause #2: identifier=ip:email combined with K8s ingress load-balancing (two observed backend peer IPs) meant each request had a different key so count never reached 5. Mitigation: normalise last_at to UTC when naive, and use email-only identifier for the lockout key. After fix, pytest TestBruteForce and the full 20-case suite pass.
